chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Every juice that is hit by fire is prohibited until two-thirds of it goes away and one-third remains.

key_terms.عَصِيرٍ: Juice (specifically grape juice in this context)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on grape juice exposed to fire in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the specific condition under which fire-exposed grape juice transitions from haram to halal, emphasizing the principle of 'kathrah' (abundance) where the remaining volume becomes sufficient for consumption. This ruling is central to Shia fiqh regarding 'nabidh' and fruit juices, distinguishing it from wine by focusing on the quantity of the original liquid rather than just the fermentation process. It reflects the juristic approach of evaluating physical changes in substances to determine their purity and permissibility.
